2010.simple: A big windowless building full of computers in tall cupboards, in a bigger city further away than today’s. Lots of companies rent rooms in it. Tap it to look inside!
2010.technical: A colocation centre in a bigger city: the video company rents a caged row of racks in a shared hall, and a cross-connect joins it to the exchange. Inside: a core router, a load balancer and a three-tier tree of switches. Tap to unfold it.

inside.simple: Your parcel comes in through the building’s front door, the core router. A traffic warden picks a computer that isn’t busy, a big switch in the middle sends the parcel down to the right cupboard, and the cupboard’s switch hands it to the video server on a copper cable. If the server doesn’t have the video yet, it fetches it from the main copy far away.
inside.technical: A rented cage at a colocation centre: the core router takes the cross-connect from the exchange, a hardware load balancer holds the service address (VIP), and a three-tier tree (core, aggregation, access) reaches the racks, with 10G fibre between the switches and 1G copper to the servers. Spanning tree keeps each rack’s second uplink blocked. A cache miss goes back to the origin.

describe.simple: Inside a big hall with a tiled floor stands a row of grey cupboards behind a wire fence, with a cooling machine at each end. The path comes from the exchange to the core router, the load balancer, an aggregation switch, a rack switch and the video server. A dashed road leads far away to the main copy. Parcels go in and video comes back out.
describe.technical: The colocation view starts at the IXP and zigzags through the core router, load balancer, aggregation switch and access switch over 10G multimode fibre, then over 1000BASE-T copper to the cache server. A caged row of racks with a CRAC unit at each end stands in the back. A dashed branch from the cache leads to the origin. Request and video packets move in opposite directions.
